overview: This five-page confidential file concerns the discovery and preliminary assessment of the Oshirabetsu graphite deposit in Hokkaido in 1948. A despatch from U.S. Political Adviser William J. Sebald forwards a Nippon Times article claiming that the deposit was the world’s second largest after Ceylon’s and a technical memorandum prepared by the Natural Resources Section of General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers. The memorandum describes the mine’s location, history, geology, mining methods, estimated reserves, output, stocks, and transportation problems, while cautioning that prospecting remained incomplete and that the Japanese claim about the deposit’s global importance could not yet be verified.

subfiles.title: Despatch forwarding reports on the Oshirabetsu graphite discovery
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards a newspaper article and a SCAP technical memorandum concerning the reported discovery of Japan’s first major graphite deposit.
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards a 1948 Nippon Times article and SCAP memo on the Oshirabetsu graphite find, noting officials couldn't verify Japan's claim it's the world's second-largest deposit.

subfiles.title: Nippon Times article, “Graphite Mine Located”
subfiles.about: The article announces the discovery of a large graphite deposit at Oshirabetsu in Hokkaido and presents official claims about its size.
subfiles.summary: Article reports the Oshirabetsu graphite deposit near Hiroo holds over 100,000 tons, ranking second only to Ceylon's, developed by Japan Carbon Company after 1947 discovery.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for Record on the Oshirabetsu Graphite Mine
subfiles.from: Hideshiro Hasegawa, Scientific Consultant, Mining and Geology Division, Natural Resources Section
subfiles.about: The memorandum provides a preliminary technical assessment of the Oshirabetsu mine’s location, geology, workings, reserves, production, stocks, and transportation limitations.
subfiles.summary: Memo details the Oshirabetsu graphite ore (about 26% carbon) in four lenticular bodies, estimating roughly 160,000 tons of reserves via electromagnetic prospecting, with open-pit mining limited by scarce ferry capacity and no on-site flotation plant.

interest: Shows SCAP evaluating a 1948 Japanese graphite discovery claim, limited by unfinished surveys and poor ferry access.
